over a fixed field $F\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let $K:X\to X$ be a compact operator
([[def-compact-linear-operator]]) and put $A:=I-K$. Then:

1. $A$ is injective if and only if it is surjective, and in that case $A$ is
   boundedly invertible;
2. for every $y\in X$ the equation $Ax=y$ has a solution if and only if
   $\varphi(y)=0$ for every $\varphi\in\ker A^*$, the transpose
   $A^*=I-K^*$ acting on $X^*$
   ([[def-transpose-of-a-bounded-operator]]);
3. $\ker A$ and the cokernel $X/\operatorname{ran}A$
   ([[def-quotient-vector-space-coset-notation]]) are finite dimensional with
   equal dimensions over $F$ ([[def-dimension]]).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\partial\Omega$ carry the
chart-independent surface measure of
[[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]] and
[[lem-surface-integral-is-independent-of-c-one-boundary-charts]], let
$1\le p<\infty$ and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then there is a
unique bounded linear operator
$$T:W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow L^p(\partial\Omega;\mathbb K)$$
with $Tu=u|_{\partial\Omega}$ for every
$u\in C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and it satisfies
$\|Tu\|_{L^p(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)}$. On each
boundary chart the operator is the flat half-space trace of
[[thm-trace-estimate-on-the-half-space]] transported by the flattening
diffeomorphism, and the chartwise definitions agree on overlaps; uniqueness
holds because two bounded operators agreeing on the dense subspace
$C(\overline\Omega)\cap W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ are equal.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$, $p'=p/(p-1)$,
$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, $v\in W^{1,p'}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and let
$T$ be the trace of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] with
$\nu$ the outward normal of
[[def-bounded-c-one-domain-boundary-charts-and-outward-normal]]. Then for
every $i=1,\dots,n$,
$$\int_\Omega u\,\partial_iv\,dx=-\int_\Omega(\partial_iu)v\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega}(Tu)(Tv)\,\nu_i\,dS,$$
and all three integrals are finite. If $u,v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the
boundary term is the classical $\int_{\partial\Omega}uv\,\nu_i\,dS$ of the
divergence theorem
[[thm-divergence-theorem-for-bounded-c-one-euclidean-domains]] applied to the
field $uv\,e_i$; if in addition $Tu=\partial_\nu w$ on $\partial\Omega$ for a specified $w\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, the boundary term is $\int_{\partial\Omega}(\partial_\nu w)(Tv)\nu_i\,dS$. The normal derivative of [[def-classical-normal-derivative]] is defined on the boundary, and this extra identity is an assumption, not an interior substitution.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, $d=n-1$, $1\le p<\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$H=\{x=(x',x_n)\in\mathbb R^n:x_n>0\}$ with
$\partial H=\mathbb R^d\times\{0\}$. Write $\partial_n$ for the last
coordinate derivative.

(i) For every $u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)$ with compact
support, the classical boundary function $g=u(\cdot,0)$ satisfies
$$|g(x')|^p\le p\int_0^\infty|u(x',t)|^{p-1}\,|\partial_nu(x',t)|\,dt$$
for a.e. $x'\in\mathbb R^d$, hence
$\|g\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}^p\le p\,\|u\|_{L^p(H)}^{p-1}\|\partial_nu\|_{L^p(H)}\le p\,\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}^p$.
For every $h>0$ the strip form
$$h\,|g(x')|^p\le C_p\Bigl(\int_0^h|u(x',t)|^pdt+h^p\int_0^h|\partial_nu(x',t)|^pdt\Bigr)$$
holds for a.e. $x'$, with $C_p=2^{p-1}$ for $1<p<\infty$ and $C_1=1$.

(ii) There is a unique bounded linear operator
$T_+:W^{1,p}(H;\mathbb K)\to L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb K)$ with
$T_+u=u(\cdot,0)$ for every compactly supported
$u\in C(\overline H)\cap W^{1,p}(H)$, and
$\|T_+u\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^d)}\le C(n,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(H)}$; it is the unique
bounded extension of classical restriction, and $T_+u$ depends only on the
a.e. class of $u$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $k\ge1$, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded $C^k$ domain in the graph sense of
[[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Then for every open set
$V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ there is a bounded
linear extension operator
$$E:W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)\longrightarrow W^{k,p}(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb K),\qquad (Eu)|_\Omega=u\ \text{a.e. on }\Omega,$$
such that $\operatorname{supp}(Eu)$ is a compact subset of $V$ for every
$u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. In particular each bounded $C^k$ domain is a
$W^{k,p}$-extension domain, with an operator whose output is supported in any
prescribed neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$. For $k=0$, extension by zero
is an isometric $L^p$ extension on any open $\Omega$; its output is supported
in the compact set $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$ when $\Omega$ is bounded.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be a
bounded extension domain, let $1\le p<n$ and $p^{*}=\frac{np}{n-p}$. Then for
every $1\le q<p^{*}$ the inclusion $W^{1,p}(\Omega)\hookrightarrow L^q(\Omega)$
is bounded and compact: every sequence bounded in $W^{1,p}(\Omega)$ has a
subsequence converging in $L^q(\Omega)$.

Let $X$ and $Y$ be normed spaces over the same field
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, read in the real case from
[[def-norm-and-normed-space]] and in the complex case from
[[rem-real-and-complex-normed-space-convention]], and suppose $X\subseteq Y$
with **continuous inclusion** $J:X\to Y$: there is a real $C\ge0$ with
$\|x\|_Y\le C\|x\|_X$ for every $x\in X$.

One says that $X$ is **compactly embedded** in $Y$, written $X\Subset Y$, when
the inclusion operator $J$ is a compact operator in the sense of
[[def-compact-linear-operator]]: the image under $J$ of every bounded
subset of $X$ ([[def-metric-bounded-diameter]]) has compact closure in $Y$
([[def-metric-compactness]]).

**The sequential form.** Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice
([[def-countable-choice]]) and the Axiom of Dependent Choice
([[def-dependent-choice]]). Then $X\Subset Y$ if and only if every bounded
sequence $(x_j)$ in $X$ has a subsequence $(x_{j_k})$ converging in $Y$:
Indeed, compact closure gives the sequence conclusion by
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]]. Conversely, fix bounded $B\subseteq X$
and let $K=\overline{J(B)}$. For any sequence $(y_j)$ in $K$, Countable
Choice selects $b_j\in B$ with $\|y_j-b_j\|_Y<1/j$ (start at $j=1$);
a convergent subsequence of $(b_j)$ gives one of $(y_j)$ with the same limit,
which belongs to the closed set $K$. Thus $K$ is sequentially compact and
[[thm-metric-compactness-equivalences]] makes it compact. The empty case is
immediate. Both readings
of $X\Subset Y$ are used on this page; the second is the form in which the
compactness theorems below are stated.

Continuity of the inclusion is a separate hypothesis and is never inferred
from compactness: a compact operator is bounded by
[[def-compact-linear-operator]] and [[def-bounded-linear-operator]], but the
definition above fixes the continuity of $J$ in advance. On this page the
continuity of every Sobolev inclusion is verified separately, through the
corresponding Sobolev embedding theorem.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $1\le p\le\infty$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^n;\mathbb R)$ with
$M_\eta:=\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty(\mathbb R^n)}$ and compact support; the case
$\eta\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is read by extending $\eta$ by zero.
Then for every $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ and every $h\ne0$, on the shrunken set
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ of
[[def-first-difference-quotient]] one has the exact identity
$$\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu=(\delta_h^i\eta)\,(\tau_{-he_i}u)\qquad\text{a.e. on }\Omega_{i,h},$$
where $\tau$ is the published translation $\tau_hu(x)=u(x-h)$ of
[[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]], so that
$(\tau_{-he_i}u)(x)=u(x+he_i)$. Consequently
$$\|\delta_h^i(\eta u)-\eta\,\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|\tau_{-he_i}u\|_{L^p(\Omega_{i,h})}\le M_\eta\,\|u\|_{L^p(\Omega)},$$
and more generally, on the domain where both sides are defined,
$$\delta_h^i\big(\eta^2\delta_h^iu\big)=\eta^2\delta_h^i\delta_h^iu+(\delta_h^i\eta^2)\,(\tau_{-he_i}\delta_h^iu).$$
The statement is quantitative in $\|D\eta\|_{L^\infty}$ and does not assume
any regularity of $u$ beyond $W^{1,p}$.

**Sobolev multiplier and support facts used below.** For every integer
$m\ge0$, $q\in W^{m,\infty}(U)$ and $z\in H^m(U)$ on an open set $U$,
$qz\in H^m(U)$ and
$$D^\alpha(qz)=\sum_{\beta\le\alpha}{\alpha\choose\beta}(D^\beta q)D^{\alpha-\beta}z,\qquad |\alpha|\le m,$$
with $\|qz\|_{H^m(U)}\le C(n,m)\|q\|_{W^{m,\infty}(U)}\|z\|_{H^m(U)}$.
Also, every compactly supported $z\in H^m(U)$ lies in $H^m_0(U)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega$ be a bounded $W^{k,p}$-extension domain, $k\ge1$ and $1\le p<\infty$. Let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $u\in W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Then:

1. if $kp<n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every $q$ with $\frac1q\ge\frac1p-\frac kn$ (equivalently $1\le q\le\frac{np}{n-kp}$);
2. if $kp=n$, $\|u\|_{L^q(\Omega)}\le C(q)\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$ for every finite $q$;
3. if $kp>n$, then for every integer $m\ge0$ and every $0<\alpha<1$ with $m+\alpha<k-\frac np$ there is a representative in $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ with $\|u\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}\le C\|u\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}$; when $k-\frac np\notin\mathbb Z$ one may take $m=\lfloor k-\frac np\rfloor$ and $\alpha=k-\frac np-m$.

Here $C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)$ uses the continuous derivatives of the constructed representative on an ambient neighbourhood of $\overline\Omega$, with norm
$$\|g\|_{C^{m,\alpha}(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\beta|\le m}\sup_{\overline\Omega}|D^\beta g|+\sum_{|\beta|=m}\sup_{\substack{x,y\in\overline\Omega\\x\ne y}}\frac{|D^\beta g(x)-D^\beta g(y)|}{|x-y|^\alpha}.$$
For $\Omega=\varnothing$ set these norm values to $0$. The proof supplies such an ambient representative, so no boundary differentiability or regularity of $\partial\Omega$ is assumed.

If $f,g\in\mathcal L^2(\mu)$, then

$$\int |fg|\,d\mu\le\|f\|_2\|g\|_2.$$

Equality holds if and only if at least one of $f,g$ is zero almost everywhere,
or there is a constant $c>0$ with

$$|f|^2=c\,|g|^2\qquad\mu\text{-almost everywhere}.$$
If $f$ is $C^2$ on an open subset of $\mathbb R^m$, then $\partial_i\partial_j f=\partial_j\partial_i f$ for every pair of coordinate indices.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$ and $\theta=1-1/p$, with
$W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ as in
[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]. Then the trace
operator $T$ of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] satisfies
$$\|Tu\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)} \qquad(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)),$$
and it is onto: $T(W^{1,p}(\Omega))=W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$. For $p>1$
the range is a strict subset of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace is not a
compact operator into $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice, used to invoke the published real and complex
$L^p$ completeness results through their Countable-Choice interface. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$,
$1\le p\le\infty$, and $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$. Then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, equipped with the displayed norm of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], is a complete normed space over
$\mathbb K$.

Both endpoints $p=1$ and $p=\infty$ are included, as is $k=0$, where the
assertion reduces to the completeness of $L^p$. If $\Omega=\varnothing$, then
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ is the zero space and the assertion is trivial.
The Axiom of Choice is used only to derive Countable Choice for the two
published completeness interfaces; no other selection is made. Representative
selection inside the finitely many coordinate classes is finite and
choice-free.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a **bounded smooth graph domain**: a nonempty bounded open set such that for every $x\in\partial\Omega$ there are an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ of $x$, a rigid motion $R(p)=Qp+b$, an open ball $B\subseteq\mathbb R^2$ and a function $h\in C^\infty(B;\mathbb R)$ such that, after shrinking $W$ so that $R(W)\subseteq B\times\mathbb R$,

$$R(\Omega\cap W)=R(W)\cap\{(y,s)\in B\times\mathbb R:s<h(y)\},$$

which is the $C^\infty$ case of the bounded $C^k$ graph domain of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]. Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be an open set with $\overline\Omega\subseteq V$. Then there exists a real-linear operator $E_\Omega$, determined only by $\Omega$, a finite smooth atlas and fixed cutoffs, such that for every open interval $J\subseteq\mathbb R$ ([[def-interval]]) and every function $u:\Omega\times J\to\mathbb R$ that is of class $C^\infty$ on the open set $\Omega\times J$ and whose every mixed derivative $D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j u:\Omega\times J\to\mathbb R$ has a continuous extension to $\overline\Omega\times J$ ([[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]]), the function $E_\Omega u$ is of class $C^\infty$ on $\mathbb R^3\times J$, satisfies $E_\Omega u(x,\tau)=u(x,\tau)$ for all $(x,\tau)\in\overline\Omega\times J$ and

$$D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j(E_\Omega u)\big|_{\overline\Omega\times J}=\text{the continuous extension of }D^\alpha\partial_\tau^j u$$

for all multi-indices $\alpha$ and all $j\ge0$, and is spatially supported in one fixed compact subset of $V$, in the sense that there is a compact $K_\Omega\subseteq V$ with $E_\Omega u(x,\tau)=0$ for all $x\notin K_\Omega$, $\tau\in J$. In every seminorm formula below, a supremum over an empty indexing set is defined to be $0$; for a nonempty bounded family of nonnegative reals it denotes the usual least real upper bound. This convention applies also to the local seminorm formulas in the proof. For every compact $K\subseteq J$, every integer $m\ge0$ and every $j\ge0$,

$$\sup_{\tau\in K}\|\partial_\tau^j E_\Omega u(\cdot,\tau)\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}\le C_m\sup_{\tau\in K}\|\partial_\tau^j u(\cdot,\tau)\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)},$$

where $\|w\|_{C^m(\overline\Omega)}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in\overline\Omega}|D^\alpha w(x)|$ and $\|W\|_{C^m(\mathbb R^3)}:=\sum_{|\alpha|\le m}\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^3}|D^\alpha W(x)|$, and the constant $C_m$ depends only on $m$, $\Omega$, the atlas and cutoffs. The extension commutes with every time derivative: $\partial_\tau^j(E_\Omega u)=E_\Omega(\partial_\tau^j u)$ for all $j\ge0$. No bound uniform over an unbounded $J$ is asserted. Vector-valued inputs of finite dimension are extended componentwise. The construction adds no choice principle: the finite atlas is selected from the cover of all admissible smooth chart patches, finite cutoffs come from the published choice-free compact cutoff lemma, and the infinite coefficient sequence is defined by the explicit formula below. The consuming elliptic or Sobolev argument retains whatever choice principles its own suppliers declare.

Assume Countable Choice for the Sobolev interfaces used below. Let
$\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$, let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, and let
$u\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
([[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]]). For
$h\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$ and $i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$ let $e_i$ be the
$i$-th standard unit vector and put
$$\Omega_{i,h}:=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}=\Omega\cap(\Omega-he_i),$$
an open subset of $\Omega$, since it is the intersection of the open set
$\Omega$ with the preimage of $\Omega$ under the homeomorphism
$x\mapsto x+he_i$. The **$i$-th difference quotient of $u$ of size $h$** is
$$\delta_h^iu(x):=\frac{u(x+he_i)-u(x)}{h},\qquad x\in\Omega_{i,h},$$
read on the almost-everywhere classes
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]); the
**difference-quotient vector** is
$$\delta_hu:=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu),$$
defined on the open intersection $\Omega_h:=\bigcap_{i=1}^n\Omega_{i,h}$,
while each component is defined on its own shrunken set $\Omega_{i,h}$.

Throughout this page the translation notation is the published one of
[[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]], namely
$\tau_hu(x)=u(x-h)$; consequently the forward shift that occurs in the
product rule is the translate by $-he_i$:
$$u(x+he_i)=(\tau_{-he_i}u)(x),\qquad \delta_h^iu=\frac{\tau_{-he_i}u-u}{h}\quad\text{on }\Omega_{i,h}.$$

For the open upper half-space
$H=\{x_n>0\}$ and a **tangential**
index $j<n$, the translation $x\mapsto x+he_j$ maps $H$ onto $H$; hence
$\delta_h^ju$ is defined on all of $H$. For the **normal** index $n$ and
$h>0$ one has $H_{n,h}=H$ (since $x_n>0$ implies $x_n+h>0$), while for
$h<0$ one has $H_{n,h}=\{x\in H:x_n>|h|\}$, a proper subset of $H$.

**Well-definedness.** Both values $u(x)$ and $u(x+he_i)$ in the numerator are
defined for every $x\in\Omega_{i,h}$, and
$$|\delta_h^iu(x)|\le\frac{|u(x+he_i)|+|u(x)|}{|h|},$$
so $\delta_h^iu\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega_{i,h};\mathbb K)$: on a compact
$K\Subset\Omega_{i,h}$ the first term is controlled by
$\int_K|u(x+he_i)|\,dx=\int_{K+he_i}|u(y)|\,dy<\infty$, because
$K+he_i$ is a compact subset of $\Omega$, and the second term is controlled
on $K\Subset\Omega$. Further, the definition depends only on the class of
$u$: if $u=\widetilde u$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$ and $E\subseteq\Omega$
is a null set with $u=\widetilde u$ on $\Omega\setminus E$, then
$\delta_h^iu\ne\delta_h^i\widetilde u$ only at points of
$(\Omega_{i,h}\cap E)\cup(\Omega_{i,h}\cap(E-he_i))$, a null set because
$E$ is null and $E-he_i$ is null by the choice-free translation invariance of
Lebesgue measure
([[thm-lebesgue-outer-measure-and-measurability-are-translation-invariant]]).

**Two warnings, part of the definition.** First, a difference quotient is
defined on the shrunken set $\Omega_{i,h}$ inside $\Omega$, which may equal
$\Omega$ when the shift preserves it; in particular it may be undefined on a strip of width $|h|$
along the boundary, so no estimate below differentiates a Sobolev class
across the boundary. Second, extending a class $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ by zero
does not enlarge the domain of its difference quotient: the quotient of the
extension agrees with $\delta_h^iu$ on $\Omega_{i,h}$, while values outside
$\Omega_{i,h}$ use points not both in $\Omega$ and are not values of the
original quotient. In the upper half-space, $\Omega_{n,h}=H$ for $h>0$,
whereas $\Omega_{n,h}=\{x\in H:x_n>|h|\}$ for $h<0$. This is why every
boundary argument on this page uses only
tangential quotients of compactly supported localisations, for which the
shrunken domain is the whole half-space and no extension across
$\partial\Omega$ is invoked.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with $n\ge1$,
let $\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, and fix $h\ne0$ and
$i\in\{1,\dots,n\}$. Write
$\Omega_{i,h}=\{x\in\Omega:x+he_i\in\Omega\}$ and
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\{x\in\Omega:x-he_i\in\Omega\}$
([[def-first-difference-quotient]]), so that
$\Omega_{i,-h}=\Omega_{i,h}+he_i$. Then:

(i) **Integration by parts, two-domain form.** Whenever the displayed
integrals converge absolutely,
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx+\frac1h\Big(\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx-\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx\Big).$$
Consequently, if
$$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}uv\,dx=\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}uv\,dx,$$
in particular if $uv$ vanishes almost everywhere outside
$\Omega_{i,h}\cap\Omega_{i,-h}$ — for instance when $uv$ has compact support in
$\Omega$ and $|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\operatorname{supp}(uv),\partial\Omega)$
— or if $\Omega_{i,h}=\Omega_{i,-h}$, then
$\int_{\Omega_{i,h}}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\Omega_{i,-h}}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx$,
with the integrals taken over their respective shrunken sets. For $\Omega=\mathbb R^n$
and $u\in L^p(\Omega)$, $v\in L^{p'}(\Omega)$ with $1\le p\le\infty$ and
$p'$ the Hölder conjugate exponent of [[def-conjugate-exponents]]
($1/p+1/p'=1$), both sides are absolutely convergent and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n}\delta_h^iu\,v\,dx=-\int_{\mathbb R^n}u\,\delta_{-h}^iv\,dx.$$

(ii) **Product rule.** If $uv\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, then a.e. on
$\Omega_{i,h}$,
$$\delta_h^i(uv)=\big(\tau_{-he_i}u\big)\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\,v=u\,\delta_h^iv+\big(\delta_h^iu\big)\big(\tau_{-he_i}v\big),$$
with the translation $\tau_{-he_i}$ of [[def-translation-of-a-function-on-rn]].
The identity is a pointwise a.e. algebraic identity; no local integrability of
its shifted cross-products is asserted beyond the hypothesis $uv\in L^1_{\rm loc}$,
which makes the left side well defined.

(iii) **Commutation with weak derivatives.** If $u$ and all its weak
derivatives $D^\gamma u$ with $|\gamma|\le|\alpha|$ have locally integrable
representatives on $\Omega$
([[def-weak-derivative-of-a-locally-integrable-function]]), then
$$D^\alpha(\delta_h^iu)=\delta_h^i(D^\alpha u)\qquad\text{weakly on }\Omega_{i,h}.$$

All identities are identities of almost-everywhere classes
([[def-l-p-space-as-a-quotient-by-null-functions]]), and the proof uses no
choice beyond the Sobolev interfaces.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$,
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$ and $\Omega'\Subset\Omega$;
write $\delta_hu=(\delta_h^1u,\dots,\delta_h^nu)$ and
$Du=(D_1u,\dots,D_nu)$ for the difference-quotient and gradient vectors, with
$$\|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|\delta_h^iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega')},\qquad \|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)}:=\Big\|\Big(\sum_{i=1}^n|D_iu|^2\Big)^{1/2}\Big\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
(1) If $1\le p\le\infty$ and $u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$, then for every
$0<|h|<\operatorname{dist}(\Omega',\partial\Omega)$ and every coordinate
direction $i$,
$$\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega)},\qquad \|\delta_hu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le n^{|1/p-1/2|}\|Du\|_{L^p(\Omega)} .$$
At $p=2$ the vector estimate has constant one. The coordinate bound also
holds on any open $U\subseteq\Omega$ for a fixed $i,h$ for which every
segment $[x,x+he_i]$, $x\in U$, stays in $\Omega$; compact containment
is unnecessary. In particular, $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(H)}\le
\|D_iu\|_{L^p(H)}$ for tangential directions on a half-space $H$.

with $\|\delta_h^iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$ for every coordinate $i$ and all

$u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega')$ with $D_iu\in L^p(\Omega')$,
$\|D_iu\|_{L^p(\Omega')}\le C$, and

Assume countable choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $S\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be an embedded smooth submanifold. Then there is a
positive smooth function $\delta:S\to(0,\infty)$ such that the restricted
normal addition map
$$E:\Omega_\delta\to\mathbb R^m,\qquad \Omega_\delta:=\{(p,v)\in N^\perp S:\|v\|<\delta(p)\},$$
is a diffeomorphism onto an open neighbourhood of $S$. In particular, $S$ has a
tubular neighbourhood in $\mathbb R^m$.

For $l\in\mathbb N_0$ and $z>0$ set

$$h_l(z)=(-i)^{l+1}\frac{e^{iz}}{z}\sum_{j=0}^{l}\frac{i^j\,(l+j)!}{j!\,(l-j)!\,(2z)^j}.$$

Then $h_l$ is a complex-valued $C^2$ function of $z>0$ solving

$$h_l''(z)+\frac2z h_l'(z)+\Bigl[1-\frac{l(l+1)}{z^2}\Bigr]h_l(z)=0,$$

it never vanishes on $(0,\infty)$, and its Wronskian-type identity $\operatorname{Im}\bigl(\overline{h_l(z)}\,h_l'(z)\bigr)=z^{-2}$ holds. For $k>0$ and $R>0$ the spherical Dirichlet-to-Neumann coefficient

$$t_l=\frac{k\,h_l'(kR)}{h_l(kR)}$$

satisfies the exact bounds

$$\operatorname{Re}t_l\le-\frac1R,\qquad |\operatorname{Re}t_l|\le\frac{l+1}{R},\qquad 0<\operatorname{Im}t_l\le k .$$

These are exact identities and inequalities for the displayed explicit functions, not asymptotic formulas; the argument uses only elementary differentiation and a constant Wronskian, so no large-$l$ asymptotic input is required.

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $\mathcal P_l$ denote the real vector space of homogeneous polynomials of degree $l$ on $\mathbb R^3$ ([[def-homogeneous-polynomial-and-homogeneous-ideal]], [[def-monomials-multidegree-and-total-degree]]), $H_l=\ker(\Delta:\mathcal P_l\to\mathcal P_{l-2})$ with $\mathcal P_k=\{0\}$ for $k<0$, and let spherical harmonics of degree $l$ be the restrictions of $H_l$ to $S^2$, with unnormalised surface measure $d\Omega$ of total mass $4\pi$ ([[def-surface-integral-on-a-compact-c-one-hypersurface]], [[lem-euclidean-chart-measure-agrees-with-polar-surface-measure]]). Then $\mathcal P_l=H_l\oplus|x|^2\mathcal P_{l-2}$, $\dim H_l=2l+1$, harmonics of distinct degree are orthogonal in $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$, and the union over $l$ of the spaces of spherical harmonics admits a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2(S^2,d\Omega)$ ([[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]). For any real orthonormal basis $Y_{lm}$, $m=1,\dots,2l+1$, of degree-$l$ harmonics the addition theorem holds:

$$\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}Y_{lm}(n)Y_{lm}(n')=\frac{2l+1}{4\pi}P_l(n\cdot n'),$$

where $P_l$ is the Legendre polynomial of the convergent zonal kernel lemma ([[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]). The Laplacian is the Euclidean one ([[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]). This supplies the harmonic decomposition, orthogonality, completeness and exact addition kernel; it does not assert higher boundary regularity. The purely polynomial decomposition and finite dimension identities use no Choice; the surface/$L^2$/completeness claims retain the stated Countable Choice.

abla(u\chi)\|_{L^2(A)}^2)$ for every smooth $u$; choosing $h$ so small that $2Ch\le\delta$, expanding $

**Coercivity of the shifted form.** With $\lambda:=\|\kappa\|_\infty(1+C_1)+k^2+1$, where $C_1$ is the constant of step 1.2 for $\delta:=\tfrac12(\|\kappa\|_\infty+1)^{-1}$, one has $\operatorname{Re}(a(E,E)+\lambda\|E\|_{L^2(A)}^2)\ge c\|E\|_{H^1(A)}^2$ for every $E\in X$, with $c=\tfrac12$. The geometric tail estimate makes $(x_n)$ Cauchy; completeness supplies its limit $x$, continuity gives $x=(I-tS)x+tf$ and $Sx=f$, and the same contraction inequality makes the fixed point unique. A conjugate-linear functional in $v$ is represented here by applying [L8] to its complex conjugate and then conjugating the pairing, so this identification is linear in $x$. The inclusion $X\hookrightarrow H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$ is continuous and $A$ is a bounded $W^{1,2}$-extension domain [L13], so by [L14] with $p=2<n=3$ every bounded sequence in $H^1(A)$ has an $L^2$-convergent subsequence; by [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice assumptions of the sequential criterion [L15] are available, so the inclusion $H^1(A)\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$ is compact, and so is its restriction $X\hookrightarrow L^2(A)$, hence also the composition $J$ of that restriction with the bounded represented pairing $L^2(A)\to X$. Therefore $K:=S^{-1}J:X\to X$ is compact, and the operator $A_{\mathrm{op}}:=S-\lambda J$ represented by $a$ satisfies $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$; by the Fredholm alternative [L9] the operator $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}$ is boundedly invertible as soon as its kernel is trivial, and its kernel consists exactly of the $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=0$ for all $v\in X$.

**Bounded invertibility of $a$.** By step 3.2 the kernel of $S^{-1}A_{\mathrm{op}}=I-\lambda K$ is trivial, so the Fredholm alternative [L9] makes it boundedly invertible; hence $A_{\mathrm{op}}=S(I-\lambda K)$ and the form $a$ are boundedly invertible: for every bounded conjugate-linear functional $F$ on $X$ there is exactly one $E\in X$ with $a(E,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$, and $\|E\|_{H^1(A)}\le C\|F\|_{X^*}$.

**The weak solution with prescribed tangential trace.** Define on $X$ the functional $F(v):=-a(G,v)-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS$. By step 5.1 there is exactly one $u\in X$ with $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for all $v\in X$; set $E:=G+u\in H^1(A;\mathbb C^3)$. Then $E_{\text{tangential}}=e_T$ on $\partial O$ because $u\in X$ and $G$ is tangential there, and testing the defining identity with $v$ compactly supported in the interior of $A$ gives $-\Delta E=k^2E$ weakly on $A$. Moreover, for every $v\in X$ supported away from $\partial O$ one has $a(E,v)=a(G,v)+a(u,v)=-\int_{\partial O}(\operatorname{div}_{\partial O}e_T)\overline{v_n}\,dS=0$, so the same integration-by-parts computation as in step 3.2 shows that the normal trace of $E$ on $S_R$ equals $T_Rf$ in the weak trace sense, where $f=E|_{S_R}=u|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}(S_R;\mathbb C^3)$.

**Gluing across the artificial sphere and smoothness on the open set $D$.** Let $E_{\mathrm{out}}$ be the outgoing series of [L1] built from the trace $f=E|_{S_R}$, defined on $\{|x|>R\}$; by [L1] it is a finite-local-energy solution there with normal derivative $T_Rf$, and it is smooth away from the sphere. The two pieces have the same trace $f$ on $S_R$; applying the Sobolev-Gauss-Green formula [L11] on $A$ and on the exterior annulus $B_M\setminus\overline B_R$ (with the outward normals $+n$ and $-n$ on $S_R$) and adding, the two interface pairings cancel, so $\widetilde E\in H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ with weak gradient the two-sided gradient. Since $k^2\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $k$ as soon as $\widetilde E\in H^k_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$, repeated application of the interior gain-two estimate [L7] starting from $H^1_{\mathrm{loc}}$ gives $\widetilde E\in H^m_{\mathrm{loc}}(D)$ for every $m$, hence a $C^\infty(D)$ representative satisfying the classical Helmholtz equation on $D$.

abla W\|_2^2+C_\epsilon(\|U\|_{H^1}^2+\|f\|_{L^2}^2+\|G\|_{H^1}^2)$ using [L17], the increment estimate $\|\delta_h^kU\|_{L^2}\le\|\partial_kU\|_{L^2}$, and [L19]. Applying step 8.1 to $Z$ gains two further tangential or mixed derivatives, and differentiating the normal-recovery equation of step 8.1 and inducting on the number of normal derivatives recovers the remaining ones; nested half-boxes and a finite boundary cover give $U\in H^m$ on each smaller patch for every $m$, with constants depending on the data, $\kappa$, the chart and the fixed nested covers. **The divergence constraint.** Let $q:=\operatorname{div}E$ on $D$. The Cartesian derivative therefore is $\partial_i[h_l(kr)Y_{lm}(n)]=-k h_{l+1}(kr)J_i(n)+k h_{l-1}(kr)\partial_iH_l(n)/(2l+1)$ for $l\ge1$; for $l=0$ only the first term occurs, since $h_0'=-h_1$ and $\partial_iH_0=0$. Since $q$ is smooth across $S_R$, its coefficients and radial derivatives extend continuously to $R$; nonvanishing of $h_j(kR)$ [L23] identifies those coefficients with the outgoing series for $q|_{S_R}$ and gives $\partial_rq=T_R(q|_{S_R})$. Thus $q$ belongs to the exact outgoing class of [L1]. The exterior scalar uniqueness lemma [L2] applies to $q$ on the connected $D$ and gives $q=0$ on $D$, that is, the divergence constraint.

**Uniqueness of the classical problem.** Let $E_1,E_2\in C^\infty(\overline D;\mathbb C^3)$ both satisfy the conditions of the Statement. Their difference $W:=E_1-E_2$ is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$, solves $(\Delta+k^2)W=0$ componentwise on $D$, has $\operatorname{div}W=0$ and $W_{\text{tangential}}=0$ on $\partial O$, and is outgoing on $S_R$. Then $W\in X$ with $W|_{S_R}\in H^{1/2}$, and the integration by parts of step 3.2 and step 6.1 shows that $a(W,v)=0$ for every $v\in X$: the volume terms reproduce the Helmholtz equation, the inner boundary term cancels against $\operatorname{div}W=0$ on $\partial O$ through the exact identity of step 10.1, and the outer term cancels because $\partial_rW=T_R(W|_{S_R})$ by outgoingness. By step 3.2, $W=0$ on $A$; its trace on $S_R$ is zero, so [L1] gives $W=0$ outside that sphere as well, hence on $D$.

**Assembly and choice accounting.** Existence is step 6.1 together with the regularity and gluing of steps 7.1, 8.1 and 9.1: the constructed $E=G+u$ has the prescribed tangential trace, satisfies $(\Delta+k^2)E=0$ on $D$, is $C^\infty$ on $\overline D$ and outgoing on $S_R$ in the stated weak trace sense, and satisfies the closure relation of step 9.1; its divergence vanishes by step 10.1. Uniqueness is step 11.1. The only choice principle used is the Axiom of Choice assumed in the Statement: it supplies the Fredholm alternative, and through [L16] the Countable and Dependent Choice invoked by the compactness, trace and difference-quotient interfaces [L15], [L10], [L12], [L17]; the lift, the coercive inversion and the boundary bootstrap make only finitely many explicit selections. This proves all assertions.

boundaries.evidence: The empty tangential datum case is the homogeneous problem: e_T=0 makes the lift G of step 1.3 zero, and the kernel analysis of steps 3.2 and 5.1 gives the identically zero solution, consistent with the existence and uniqueness claims.
The zero datum returns u=0 through steps 1.3, 5.1 and 6.1; uniqueness in step 11.1 then forces every solution with zero tangential trace and the closure relation to be zero.

A single nonzero tangential mode cannot survive the homogeneous kernel: the imaginary part of the form in step 3.2 forces the full trace f=0 on S_R, and the extension argument of that step then gives the zero solution.

Statement and proof: Smooth compact boundary permits the normal collar and local frames; k>0 and R>0, with obstacle closure strictly inside B_R, avoid boundary intersections. Connected exterior D is used in the kernel UCP and in final scalar divergence uniqueness.
Statement and proof: Degree zero in outgoing differentiation uses h_0 prime=-h_1 and zero derivative of its constant solid harmonic; there is no undefined h_{-1}. All k,R are strictly positive.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the trace and Sobolev suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be a measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic coefficient as in the lift lemma ([[lem-em-lift-specified-dirichlet-existence]]), let $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and prescribe $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)=W^{1/2,2}(\partial\Omega)$, the fractional Sobolev space of the boundary definition, defined by a finite graph atlas and partition with norm given by the finite sums of localised $L^2$ norms and Gagliardo seminorms ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). Then there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ solving

$$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho\,v\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega),$$

and the solution depends continuously on $(\rho,g)$: $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$. The prescribed trace is exact and no classical $C^2$ boundary regularity is inferred.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice inherited from the stated weak-existence, Sobolev extension and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain ([[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]), let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, and let $\rho$ be smooth on the closure. Prescribe in the prescribed-data lemma either smooth Dirichlet data $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$, or smooth outward flux data $g$ with its compatibility condition as in the weak Neumann lemma. Then the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with those data is $C^\infty$ on the closure $\overline\Omega$. For finitely many disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $\rho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$, the weak solution is smooth on each closed side. Edge and junction points, reentrant corners and coefficient loss of regularity are excluded. The existence claims are those of the two weak solvability lemmas; this lemma proves their classical upgrade on the declared domains.

Assume the Axiom of Choice for the actually cited Sobolev trace, lift and mean-zero density interfaces, and its Countable Choice consequence for the measure and variational interfaces ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $\varepsilon$ be measurable symmetric uniformly elliptic ([[lem-em-prescribed-fractional-dirichlet-existence]]), let $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$, and let $g\in H^{-1/2}(\partial\Omega)$, the bounded real dual of the boundary trace space ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]). Define $\ell(v)=\int_\Omega\rho v+\langle g,Tv\rangle$ on $H^1(\Omega)$ ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]). A weak Neumann solution is a $u\in H^1$ with

$$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\ell(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H^1(\Omega).$$

Such a solution exists if and only if $\ell(1)=0$, and is then unique up to an additive constant; normalising $\int_\Omega u=0$ makes it unique. On finitely many connected components the compatibility and normalisation are imposed separately on each component. For finitely many disjoint smooth stationary interfaces with piecewise smooth uniformly elliptic $\varepsilon$, bulk data $\rho\in L^2$ and prescribed sheet charge $\sigma$ on the interfaces defining a bounded trace functional on $H^1$ (for instance $\sigma\in L^2$ of each smooth compact interface), the same argument gives weak Dirichlet or compatible Neumann existence for the transmission problem, with the globally $H^1$ potential having identical one-sided trace; where the solution is classically smooth on each side, integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$, equivalently $n\cdot[D]=\sigma$ for the explicitly defined mathematical flux $D:=-\varepsilon\nabla u$ on each side. General piecewise classical regularity remains a separate requirement.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. If Omega has the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, then $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F=\sum_j\int_{S_j}F\cdot\nu_j\,dS$, with faces counted once off E. All integrals are finite. In a specified finite gluing, the two fluxes on every shared face cancel.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a bounded $C^1$ domain or have the specified finite piecewise $C^1$ presentation. For real $u\in C^2(\overline\Omega)$ and $v\in C^1(\overline\Omega)$, $$\int_\Omega(v\Delta u+Du\cdot Dv)\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}v\partial_\nu u\,dS.$$ In the piecewise case the right side is the sum over faces, counted once off E. All integrals are finite.

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]), supplying the completeness and Countable-Choice interfaces of the two variational suppliers. Let $L>0$ and let $\Omega\subseteq(-L,L)^3$ be bounded and open, let $\varepsilon$ be a measurable symmetric real $3\times3$ matrix field on $\Omega$ with $\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le\beta|\xi|^2$ for a.e. $x$ and all $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$, $0<\alpha\le\beta<\infty$, let $G\in H^1(\Omega)$ be a specified lift, and let $F\in(H_0^1(\Omega))^*$ be bounded. Then there is exactly one $u\in G+H_0^1(\Omega)$ with

$$\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=F(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in H_0^1(\Omega),$$

where $H_0^1=W_0^{1,2}(\Omega)$ carries the gradient norm. For $F(v)=\int_\Omega\rho v$ with $\rho\in L^2(\Omega)$ this is the weak Poisson solution $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$, with the homogeneous boundary datum represented by membership of $H_0^1$ rather than by an unproved classical trace. No boundary datum outside the specified lift class is assumed attainable; classical boundary regularity, general Neumann lifts and transmission regularity remain later obligations.

Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open with
$n\ge1$, let $k\in\mathbb N_0$, let $1\le p\le\infty$, and let
$\mathbb K\in\{\mathbb R,\mathbb C\}$.

Every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ belongs to
$W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$. Indeed $\varphi$ is bounded with compact support,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ for every exponent in range, and each of
its classical partial derivatives is again smooth and compactly supported,
hence lies in $L^p(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ and is the corresponding weak derivative
by [[lem-classical-derivatives-are-weak-derivatives]].

Define the **zero-boundary Sobolev space**
$$W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K):=\overline{C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)},$$
the closure taken in the normed space
$(W^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K),\|\cdot\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)})$ of
[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. The norm is a genuine norm on classes
by [[lem-sobolev-norm-is-well-defined-and-definite]], so this is the usual
metric closure of a subset of a normed space: $u\in W_0^{k,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$
if and only if for every $\delta>0$ there is
$\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ with
$\|u-\varphi\|_{W^{k,p}(\Omega)}<\delta$. Write
$H_0^k(\Omega):=W_0^{k,2}(\Omega;\mathbb K)$ when the scalar field is fixed by
context.

Three warnings are part of the definition. First, this is a closure of
almost-everywhere classes, and all its equalities are equalities of Sobolev
classes. Second, no pointwise boundary values and no trace characterization
are asserted: a description of $W_0^{k,p}$ by vanishing boundary data belongs
to the later trace theory and is not used here. Third, the closure is defined
for every $1\le p\le\infty$, but for $p=\infty$ it is not claimed that every
compactly supported $W^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$ function lies in $W_0^{k,\infty}(\Omega)$;
the definition merely names the closure of the test functions.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge2$, be a
bounded $C^1$ domain, $1<p<\infty$ and $\theta=1-1/p$, with
$W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$ as in
[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]. Then the trace
operator $T$ of [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]] satisfies
$$\|Tu\|_{W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)}\le C(\Omega,p)\|u\|_{W^{1,p}(\Omega)} \qquad(u\in W^{1,p}(\Omega;\mathbb K)),$$
and it is onto: $T(W^{1,p}(\Omega))=W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$. For $p>1$
the range is a strict subset of $L^p(\partial\Omega)$, and the trace is not a
compact operator into $W^{\theta,p}(\partial\Omega)$.

derivations.claim: **The Dirichlet branch: existence, uniqueness, exact trace, continuous dependence.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)\subset H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ and $\rho\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega)\subset L^2(\Omega)$. By [L1] with the uniformly elliptic smooth coefficient $\varepsilon$ there is exactly one $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ and $\int_\Omega\nabla v\cdot\varepsilon\nabla u=\int_\Omega\rho v$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, and $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|\rho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$; this gives the existence, uniqueness, exact prescribed trace and continuous dependence asserted in (a).

**The Neumann branch.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ and put $\ell(v):=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$; since $g$ is bounded and $T$ is bounded into $L^2(\partial\Omega)$, $\ell$ is a bounded linear functional on $H^1(\Omega)$ of the form required by [L3] with $H^{-1/2}$ density represented by the smooth function $g$. Testing the weak identity with the constant $1$ on a component $\Omega_j$ gives $0=\int_{\Omega_j}
abla1\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\ell(1_{\Omega_j})=\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g$, so the componentwise compatibility is necessary; it is also the hypothesis of the Statement. By [L3] there is then a weak solution, unique up to one additive constant per component, and the normalisation $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ makes it unique; on each connected component the upgrade part of [L2] applies with the smooth datum $g$ and gives $C^\infty$ local classical solutions satisfying $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ and $
u\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=g$, the different choices of the additive constant changing nothing in the equation. On a connected $\Omega$ this is $0=\int_\Omegaho+\int_{\partial\Omega}g$, that is $\int_{\partial\Omega}g=-\int_\Omegaho$.

**Transmission: weak existence, unique traces and the conditional jump.** In the configuration of part (c), let $\Lambda(v):=\int_\Omega\rho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$, a bounded functional on $H^1(\Omega)$ because $\sigma$ is smooth on the compact interface union and $T$ is bounded into $L^2$ of that finite union. For outer Dirichlet data, obtain an exact $H^1$ boundary lift $G$ from [L1] applied with coefficient $I$ and zero bulk datum (this is only a lift, not the transmission solution). Restrict the bounded functional $\Lambda$ to $H_0^1$ and apply [L6] with the actual piecewise coefficient; it gives the unique transmission solution in $G+H_0^1$ with the prescribed outer trace. For outer Neumann data, the weak Neumann part of [L3] applies directly to the bounded functional including the sheet and outer flux terms; hence a globally $H^1$ weak solution exists, is unique for outer Dirichlet data, and for outer Neumann data exists exactly when $\Lambda(v)+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ vanishes on the constants of every component, that is when the stated compatibility holds, and is then unique modulo componentwise constants, the zero componentwise means fixing it. By the transmission part of [L3] the globally $H^1$ potential has identical one-sided traces, and wherever it is classically smooth on each side, integration by parts gives the jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon\nabla u]=-\sigma$ in the stated sign convention.

**Classical upgrade of the Dirichlet branch.** The solution of step 1.1 is the weak solution of $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$ in $\Omega$ with the smooth Dirichlet datum $g$: for compactly supported test fields the weak identity is exactly the distributional equation $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon\nabla u)=\rho$, where the divergence is that of a $C^1$ field once the classical upgrade below identifies $u$ as such, and the boundary values are the prescribed ones by trace uniqueness. Applying the Dirichlet part of [L2] with the smooth $\rho$ and smooth $g$ yields the $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$ satisfying the classical equation and boundary values.

**Transmission: one-sided classical regularity and the unconditional jump.** The weak solution of step 1.3 is the weak solution of the transmission problem for the piecewise smooth positive $\varepsilon$, piecewise smooth $ho$ and smooth sheet charge $\sigma$ of the Statement, with either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum or the smooth compatible outer Neumann datum. By the interface part of [L2] it is $C^\infty$ on each closed side; in particular it is classically smooth on each side of every interface, so the conditional jump identity of step 1.3 applies and the flux jump $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ holds unconditionally in the stated class. The equal one-sided traces are those of step 1.3, and on each closed side the classical equation $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ holds because the weak identity tested against compactly supported fields localized in the interior of a side is the distributional equation there. The interface integration by parts underlying the jump is the divergence theorem [L4] applied to the $C^1$ field $v\,\varepsilon
abla u$ on the two pieces and the Green identity [L5]; the smooth chain and product rules of [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]] and [[thm-chain-rule-for-total-derivatives]] are the calculus conventions used in transporting the equation to the closed pieces, and the Euclidean pairings are those of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]].

**Assembly and exclusions.** Part (a) is steps 1.1 and 2.1, part (b) is step 1.2, and part (c) is steps 1.3 and 2.2, with the definitions of the conormal vector and derivative fixed in the Statement. Nothing beyond the declared smooth-domain, finite-interface regime is asserted: no edge or junction point, no reentrant corner, no coefficient loss of regularity and no general piecewise classical regularity is claimed, and no existence assertion is used beyond the two weak solvability lemmas [L1] and [L3]. The choice assumptions are exactly those recorded in the Choice accounting paragraph, and the finite interface and component collections are handled by the explicit finite sums above. This proves all three parts.

Statement and proof: Zero bulk, boundary and sheet data give the zero normalized solution; sigma=0 imposes n dot [epsilon grad u]=0, not equality of the entire flux vector.

One connected component makes the Neumann compatibility read integral of rho plus boundary g equals zero and the single zero-mean normalisation determine the solution, as recorded in steps 1.2 and 3.1.
Uniform positivity alpha>0, beta<infinity excludes degenerate coefficients, and the Statement and step 3.1 exclude edge, junction, reentrant and coefficient-loss cases from the conclusions.
Boundary values are exact traces supplied by [L1], not endpoint limits, and no condition at infinity occurs because Omega is bounded; the interface conclusions of step 2.2 cover both closed sides.

The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice are those declared by the weak-solvability and regularity suppliers [L1]-[L3] and propagated in the choice accounting of step 3.1; the classical upgrades add no choice.
The forward direction of the Neumann criterion is proved in step 1.2: testing with the constant 1 on a component gives integral rho plus integral g = 0, so the compatibility is necessary.

The reverse direction is the existence clause of [L3] applied in steps 1.2 and 1.3: when the componentwise compatibility (including sheet charges) holds, the weak solution exists, and step 2.1 upgrades it.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice, as used by the complete variational, Sobolev-extension and compact-spectral suppliers. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain. Define $H(\operatorname{curl})=\{u\in L^2(\Omega;\mathbb R^3):\operatorname{curl}u\in L^2\}$ and $H(\operatorname{div})=\{u\in L^2:\operatorname{div}u\in L^2\}$ with their graph norms, and let $X$ be the graph-norm closure in $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$ of the smooth fields on the closure with $n\times u=0$; this is an explicit weak perfect-electric-conductor boundary class. Put $V=\{u\in X:\operatorname{div}u=0\}$ and $H=\overline{V}^{\,L^2}$. Then the curl form on $V$ has a complete orthonormal $L^2$ eigenbasis with nonnegative eigenvalues $\lambda_j$ of finite multiplicity tending to infinity whenever $H$ is infinite dimensional, and the zero eigenspace is finite dimensional and must be retained when the topology allows it. Each eigenfield $u_j\in V$ satisfies the full graph-class variational identity $\int_\Omega\operatorname{curl}u_j\cdot\operatorname{curl}v=\lambda_j\int_\Omega u_j\cdot v$ for every $v\in X$. The eigen equation is $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u_j=\lambda_ju_j$ distributionally with the PEC trace, and for every explicitly chosen mathematical speed $v_{\mathrm{wave}}>0$ and every initial displacement $q_0\in V$ and velocity $q_1\in H$, the associated second-order wave has coefficients $a_j''+v_{\mathrm{wave}}^2\lambda_ja_j=0$ with those initial coefficients. Its displacement lies in $C(\mathbb R;V)$ and its velocity in $C(\mathbb R;H)$; finite modal sums converge respectively in $C(K;V)$ and $C(K;H)$ on every compact time interval $K$. The finite-dimensional $\lambda=0$ sector is retained with $a_j(t)=a_j(0)+ta_j'(0)$. This speed is a positive abstract mathematical parameter, not a physical constant or prerequisite. No identification with every maximal tangential-trace realisation, and no lossy, open or non-smooth-domain spectral claim, is made.

For each $m$, $\|u\|_{H^m}\le C_{m,\Omega,\lambda}\|u\|_{H^1}$. The equations $\operatorname{curl}\operatorname{curl}u=\lambda u$, $\operatorname{div}u=0$, $

u u_n+(\operatorname{div}
u)u_n=0$ hold classically, where $u_n=u\cdot
u$ and the normal is extended constant along collar normal lines. This includes zero eigenvalues and disconnected domains; it asserts neither equality with every maximal tangential-trace realization nor smoothness of arbitrary finite-energy modal sums.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the weak-solvability and regularity lemmas below ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in the local graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]], let $\varepsilon\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega;\operatorname{Sym}^3)$ be uniformly positive, that is $\alpha|\xi|^2\le\xi\cdot\varepsilon(x)\xi\le eta|\xi|^2$ for all $\xi\in\mathbb R^3$ and $x\in\Omega$ and some $0<\alpha\le eta<\infty$, and let $ho$ be smooth on $\overline\Omega$. The Euclidean inner product is that of [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]; at a boundary point with outward unit normal $
u$ the outward conormal vector is $\varepsilon
u$ and the outward conormal derivative is $
u\cdot\varepsilon
abla u$. Here $\operatorname{Sym}^3$ is the space of real symmetric $3	imes3$ matrices, $H^1(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ is the Sobolev space of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], $H_0^1(\Omega)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]), and $T:H^1(\Omega)	o H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$ is the bounded onto trace of [[thm-sharp-trace-theorem-for-w-one-p]], with the fractional boundary space defined in [L1]. Then:

(a) **Dirichlet.** For every $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ there is exactly one weak solution $u\in H^1(\Omega)$ with trace $Tu=g$ of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u\,dx=\int_\Omegaho v\,dx$ for all $v\in H_0^1(\Omega)$; it depends continuously on the data, $\|u\|_{H^1}\le C(\|ho\|_{L^2}+\|g\|_{H^{1/2}})$, has a $C^\infty$ representative on $\overline\Omega$, and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon

(b) **Neumann.** Let $g\in C^\infty(\partial\Omega)$ be a smooth outward conormal datum satisfying $\int_{\Omega_j}ho\,dx+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g\,dS=0$ on every connected component $\Omega_j$ of $\Omega$. Then there is a weak solution of $\int_\Omega
abla v\cdot\varepsilon
abla u=\int_\Omegaho v+\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ for all $v\in H^1(\Omega)$; it is unique up to a separately chosen additive constant on each component, and imposing $\int_{\Omega_j}u=0$ on every component gives a unique normalised solution which is $C^\infty$ on each closed component and satisfies the classical equations $-\operatorname{div}(\varepsilon
abla u)=ho$ in $\Omega$ and $
u\cdot\varepsilon

(c) **Transmission.** Let there be finitely many pairwise disjoint closed smooth interfaces strictly inside $\Omega$, let $\varepsilon$ be piecewise smooth on the closures of the resulting pieces and uniformly positive in the above sense, let $ho$ be piecewise smooth on the closed pieces and let $\sigma$ be a smooth sheet charge on the union of the interfaces; the weak right-hand side is $\int_\Omegaho v+\sum_\Gamma\int_\Gamma\sigma\,Tv$, together with $\int_{\partial\Omega}g\,Tv$ in the Neumann case. Prescribe either the smooth outer Dirichlet datum of (a), or the smooth outer Neumann datum of (b) with the componentwise compatibility condition $\int_{\Omega_j}ho+\sum_{\Gamma\subset\Omega_j}\int_\Gamma\sigma+\int_{\partial\Omega_j}g=0$ for every component $\Omega_j$. With outer Dirichlet data the globally $H^1$ solution is unique; with outer Neumann data it exists exactly when that compatibility holds and is then unique modulo componentwise additive constants, the zero componentwise means making it unique; the equal one-sided traces and $C^\infty$ regularity on each closed side hold in either case, and the flux jump is $n\cdot[\varepsilon
abla u]=-\sigma$ in the sign convention of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]], where $n$ is a chosen unit normal on the interface and $[\varepsilon
abla u]=\varepsilon^+
abla u^+-\varepsilon^-
abla u^-$ is the difference from the $n$-positive side to the other.

Edge and junction points, reentrant corners, coefficient loss of regularity and general piecewise classical regularity beyond finitely many disjoint smooth interfaces are excluded. The existence content of all three parts is that of the two weak solvability lemmas; this theorem states the combined existence-and-regularity conclusions on the declared domains and adds no existence assertion beyond them.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $Q=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$ with $L_j>0$ and let $\varepsilon,\mu>0$ be constants. Define the reflection boundary class by extending $E_1$ evenly across the $x_1$-walls and oddly across the $x_2,x_3$-walls, and cyclically for $E_2,E_3$; extend $B_1$ oddly across $x_1$ and evenly across $x_2,x_3$, cyclically for $B_2,B_3$. Work on the rectangular torus $\prod_j\mathbb R/(2L_j\mathbb Z)$ in the real $L^2$ fields with these parities and distributional $\operatorname{div}E=\operatorname{div}B=0$. For smooth fields the parity class gives $n\times E=0$ and $n\cdot B=0$ on $\partial Q$. Then: (i) the finite separated Fourier modes are dense in this class, and the class is complete for the $L^2$ pairing ([[lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space]], [[def-orthonormal-family-complete-orthonormal-system-and-hilbert-basis]]); (ii) for every initial datum in the class there is a unique $C(\mathbb R;L^2)$ weak solution of $\partial_tE=(\varepsilon\mu)^{-1}\operatorname{curl}B$, $\partial_tB=-\operatorname{curl}E$ in the same class ([[def-distributional-derivative]]); (iii) the energy $\tfrac12\int_Q(\varepsilon|E|^2+|B|^2/\mu)\,dx$ is constant along the solution. This is an explicit weak PEC model; it supplies neither trace regularity for arbitrary $H(\operatorname{curl})$ fields nor completeness in lossy, open or non-rectangular guides.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> ([[def-choice-function]]).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of [[def-choice-function]]: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets ([[def-countable]]) has a choice function.

Let $k\in\mathbb N$, let $m,q\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^m$ be open, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$. A map $f:U\to\mathbb R^q$ is of class $C^k$ when each component is of class $C^k$. Each scalar component uses the word-derivative convention of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]], whose source dimension is positive. The map is **smooth**, or $C^\infty$, when it is $C^k$ for every $k\in\mathbb N$.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $U,V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open. A bijection $f:U\to V$ is a **$C^k$ diffeomorphism** when both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $C^k$. For $k\ge1$, a **local $C^k$ diffeomorphism at $a\in U$** is a restriction $f|_P:P\to Q$ between open neighbourhoods of $a$ and $f(a)$ that is a $C^k$ diffeomorphism. At $k=1$ this agrees with [[def-c-one-map-and-local-inverse]]: continuous first partial derivatives give the required total derivative by [[thm-continuous-partial-derivatives-imply-total-differentiability]], while continuity of the total derivative gives continuity of its matrix entries and hence of the first partial derivatives.

Let $n \in \mathbb{N}$. A natural number is a von Neumann natural, that is a set,
and $n = \{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$ ([[def-natural-numbers]],
[[lem-nat-order-is-membership]]), so

$$\mathbb{R}^{n} \;=\; \{\, x \;:\; x \text{ is a function } n \to \mathbb{R} \,\}$$

is the function space of [[def-function-space]] at $F = \mathbb{R}$ and $X = n$,
a vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ under the pointwise operations
([[def-vector-space]]). We write $x_k := x(k)$ for $k < n$, and two elements of
$\mathbb{R}^{n}$ are equal exactly when they agree at every $k < n$. This is the
same set that [[lem-metrics-on-rn]] calls $\mathbb{R}^{n}$.

The **Euclidean inner product** of $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ is the real number

$$\langle x, y\rangle \;:=\; \sum_{k<n} x_k\,y_k ,$$

the finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]] applied to the list $k \mapsto x_k y_k$
(extended by $0$ beyond $n$, as every finite list in this library is). The
**Euclidean norm** of $x$ is

$$\lVert x\rVert_2 \;:=\; \sqrt{\langle x, x\rangle},$$

which is defined because $\langle x,x\rangle = \sum_{k<n} x_k^{2} \ge 0$ (a sum
of nonnegative terms, [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4 and
[[lem-of-square-positive]], the case $x_k = 0$ giving $x_k^2 = 0$ by
[[def-integer-power]]) and every nonnegative real has a unique nonnegative square
root ([[thm-of-square-roots]]).

### Both are defined for every $n$, including $n = 0$

At $n = 0$ the set $\mathbb{R}^{0}$ has exactly one element, the empty function,
and it is the zero vector space ([[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]] clause 5); the sum
above is the empty sum, so $\langle x,y\rangle = 0$ and $\lVert x\rVert_2 = 0$.
**This is the first place on this page where the two index regimes diverge, and
the divergence is deliberate.** The published metrics $d_1$, $d_2$, $d_\infty$ of
[[lem-metrics-on-rn]] are defined only for $n \ge 1$, because $d_\infty$ would
otherwise be a maximum over the empty index set; the algebra above needs no such
restriction. The boundary in this page runs between the algebra and the metric,
not where a reader would guess, and [[rem-rn-conventions-and-scope]] lists
exactly which items inherit $n \ge 1$.

### The algebra of the inner product

For all $x, y, z \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

1. **Symmetry.** $\langle x,y\rangle = \langle y,x\rangle$, since $x_ky_k = y_kx_k$
   termwise.
2. **Additivity in the first argument.**
   $\langle x + y, z\rangle = \langle x,z\rangle + \langle y,z\rangle$: the list
   $k \mapsto (x_k+y_k)z_k$ is the termwise sum of $k \mapsto x_kz_k$ and
   $k \mapsto y_kz_k$, so [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 1 applies.
3. **Homogeneity in the first argument.**
   $\langle \lambda x, y\rangle = \lambda\langle x,y\rangle$, by
   [[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 2.
4. **Bilinearity.** Clauses 2 and 3 together with symmetry give the same two laws
   in the second argument.
5. **Positive definiteness.** $\langle x,x\rangle \ge 0$, and
   $\langle x,x\rangle = 0$ if and only if $x = 0$. Indeed a vanishing sum of
   nonnegative terms has every term $0$ ([[lem-finite-sum-laws]] clause 4), so
   $x_k^{2} = 0$ for every $k < n$, and a nonzero real has a positive square
   ([[lem-of-square-positive]]), whence $x_k = 0$ for every $k < n$ and $x = 0$.
6. **Agreement with the published Euclidean metric.** For $n \ge 1$ and
   $x, y \in \mathbb{R}^{n}$,
   $\lVert x - y\rVert_2 = \sqrt{\sum_{k<n}(x_k-y_k)^{2}} = d_2(x,y)$, the two
   sides being the same expression ([[lem-metrics-on-rn]]). In particular
   $\lVert x\rVert_2 = d_2(x, 0)$.

That $\lVert\cdot\rVert_2$ is a norm in the sense of [[def-norm-and-normed-space]]
is proved in [[thm-cauchy-schwarz-and-the-euclidean-norm]], where the triangle
inequality is obtained from the Cauchy-Schwarz inequality; it is not assumed
here.

Let $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, let $c \in A$ be a limit point of $A$
([[def-limit-point-r]]), let $f, g : A \to \mathbb{R}$ be differentiable at $c$
([[def-derivative]]) and let $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}$. Then:

1. $f + g$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(f+g)'(c) = f'(c) + g'(c)$;
2. $\alpha f$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(\alpha f)'(c) = \alpha f'(c)$;
3. $fg$ is differentiable at $c$ and $(fg)'(c) = f'(c)g(c) + f(c)g'(c)$;
4. if $g(c) \ne 0$ then, writing $A_0 := \{\, x \in A : g(x) \ne 0 \,\}$, the
   point $c$ lies in $A_0$ and is a limit point of $A_0$, the quotient
   $(f/g)|_{A_0} : A_0 \to \mathbb{R}$, $x \mapsto f(x)/g(x)$, is differentiable
   at $c$ as a function on $A_0$, and
   $$\bigl((f/g)|_{A_0}\bigr)'(c) \;=\; \frac{f'(c)\,g(c) - f(c)\,g'(c)}{g(c)^{2}} .$$

Each claim asserts two things: that the derivative on the left exists, and that
it has the stated value. Both are proved.

**Why claim 4 is stated on $A_0$.** The function $f/g$ is not defined where $g$
vanishes, and $g$ may vanish at points of $A$ far from $c$; restricting to $A_0$
is forced. That the restriction still has $c$ as a limit point, so that a
derivative there means anything at all, is not free either, and it is the last
claim of [[lem-sign-preservation-near-a-limit]] applied to $g$. The hypothesis
is $g(c) \ne 0$, not "$g$ vanishes nowhere".

**Everything is proved through
[[thm-caratheodory-characterisation]].** No difference quotient is estimated and
no limit theorem beyond continuity is used, so no choice principle is spent.
The four identities are four algebraic rearrangements of an increment, each
followed by a reading of [[thm-algebra-of-continuous-functions]].

Let $f:U\to V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be totally differentiable at $a\in U$ and let $g:V\to\mathbb R^p$ be totally differentiable at $f(a)$. Then $g\circ f$ is totally differentiable at $a$ and

$$D(g\circ f)(a)=Dg(f(a))\circ Df(a).$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $\Omega$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain in $\mathbb R^3$ in the graph sense of [[def-bounded-c-k-domain-and-boundary-charts]]; connectedness is unnecessary. Write $H^m(\Omega)=W^{m,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ with the multi-index integral norm ([[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]) and $H_0^1(\Omega)$ for the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ ([[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]]). For every real $f\in L^2(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u\in H_0^1(\Omega)\cap H^2(\Omega)$ satisfying

$$\int_\Omega(\nabla u\cdot\nabla v+uv)=\int_\Omega fv\qquad(v\in H_0^1(\Omega)).$$

It satisfies $(1-\Delta)u=f$ distributionally and almost everywhere as an $L^2$ identity, and

$$\|u\|_{H^1(\Omega)}\le\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad\|u\|_{H^2(\Omega)}\le C_\Omega\|f\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

Moreover $D=\{\varphi\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega):\varphi|_{\partial\Omega}=0\}$ is dense in $H^2(\Omega)\cap H_0^1(\Omega)$ in the $H^2$ norm: every such $w$ has $\varphi_j\in D$ with $\varphi_j\to w$ in $H^2$. Here smoothness on the closure means restriction of a smooth function on a neighbourhood of the closure, equivalently the smooth chart representatives used below. In particular $\nabla\varphi_j\to\nabla w$ in the graph norm of $H(\operatorname{curl})\cap H(\operatorname{div})$, with zero curl and $\operatorname{div}\nabla w=\Delta w$; every $\nabla\varphi_j$ is smooth and PEC since its tangential derivatives vanish at the boundary. For precision, let $X_\Omega$ be the graph-norm closure of smooth vector fields on a neighbourhood of the closure with $\nu\times v=0$ on the boundary, where $\nu$ is the outward Euclidean unit normal. The ambient graph space consists of real $L^2$ vector fields whose distributional $\operatorname{div}v=\sum_i\partial_iv_i$ and $\operatorname{curl}v=(\partial_2v_3-\partial_3v_2,\partial_3v_1-\partial_1v_3,\partial_1v_2-\partial_2v_1)$ lie in $L^2$; its norm squared is $\|v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{curl}v\|_2^2+\|\operatorname{div}v\|_2^2$. Thus $\nabla w$ belongs to this explicitly defined $X_\Omega$, the same completion used by the later cavity item. No equality with every maximal trace realisation is asserted.

No smoothness of $f$, no classical boundary value for general $u$, and no general nonsmooth-domain, Neumann, interface, or variable-coefficient claim is included. Zero boundary condition means membership in $H_0^1$; the published trace theorem identifies its trace as zero.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be $C^2$ in the sense of [[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. Then $\nabla f$ is a $C^1$ field on $U$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], since each of its components $\partial_if$ has continuous first partial derivatives, so its divergence is defined; the **Laplacian** of $f$ is

$$\Delta f:=\operatorname{div}\nabla f=\sum_{i<n}\partial_i\partial_if,$$

with the gradient of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]] and the divergence of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]. A $C^2$ function with $\Delta f=0$ on $U$ is called **harmonic** on $U$.

For a $C^2$ map $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{q-1}):U\to\mathbb R^q$, whose components are $C^2$ by [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]], $\Delta F$ is the field whose $i$th coordinate is $\Delta F_i$. In the three-coordinate naming of this page, $\Delta f=\partial_x\partial_xf+\partial_y\partial_yf+\partial_z\partial_zf$ and $\Delta F=(\Delta F_x,\Delta F_y,\Delta F_z)$.

Let $n\ge1$, let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open and let $F=(F_0,\ldots,F_{n-1}):U\to\mathbb R^n$ be $C^1$ in the componentwise Euclidean sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. Then the **divergence** of $F$ is $\operatorname{div}F:=\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i$, the function $U\to\mathbb R$ whose value at $p$ is $\sum_{i<n}\partial_iF_i(p)$. The partial derivatives are those of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the sum is the finite sum used throughout [[def-euclidean-inner-product]]. Since each $\partial_iF_i$ is continuous on $U$, so is $\operatorname{div}F$.

Now let $n=3$ and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Following [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], write the three coordinates of a point and of a vector as $x,y,z$ rather than $0,1,2$, so that $F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ means $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2)$ and $\partial_x,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2$. With that naming, the **curl** of $F$ is $\operatorname{curl}F:=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, a map $U\to\mathbb R^3$ each of whose coordinates is continuous on $U$. In this naming the divergence reads $\operatorname{div}F=\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z$.

Both operators are defined pointwise from the first partial derivatives of the components, so no differentiability of $F$ beyond $C^1$ is used and no orientation or metric structure enters beyond the standard coordinates of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]. For a $C^1$ scalar function $f$ on $U$, the gradient $\nabla f=(\partial_0f,\ldots,\partial_{n-1}f)$ is that of [[def-jacobian-matrix-and-gradient]]; in the three-coordinate naming, $\nabla f=(\partial_xf,\partial_yf,\partial_zf)$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $n \ge 1$,
let $S^{n-1} \subseteq \mathbb R^n$ be the unit sphere, and let $\sigma$ be the
set function of [[def-polar-surface-measure-on-the-unit-sphere]]. Then $\sigma$
is a finite Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$, and for every Borel measurable
$f : \mathbb R^n \to [0,\infty]$,
$$\int_{\mathbb R^n} f(x)\,d\lambda_n(x) = \int_0^\infty \int_{S^{n-1}} f(r\omega) r^{n-1}\,d\sigma(\omega)\,dr.$$
Moreover, $\sigma$ is the unique Borel measure on $S^{n-1}$ with this
property.

For $r\ge0$, put $\overline B_3(0,r):=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2\le r\}$, extending the positive-radius notation of [[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]] to $r=0$. This closed three-dimensional ball has volume $4\pi r^3/3$.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. For $n\ge2$, a bounded $C^1$ domain Omega and $F\in C^1(\overline\Omega;\mathbb R^n)$, $\int_\Omega\operatorname{div}F\,dx=\int_{\partial\Omega}F\cdot\nu\,dS$. Both integrals are finite, with the continuous interior derivative convention and the outward normal on every boundary component.

Let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be open, $n\ge1$, let
$u,v\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$, and let
$\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$ be the multi-index of
[[def-ck-and-multi-index-notation-in-several-variables]]. We say that $v$ is
the **weak derivative** $D^\alpha u$ if
$$\int_\Omega u\,D^\alpha\varphi\,dx =(-1)^{|\alpha|}\int_\Omega v\varphi\,dx \qquad\text{for every }\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega).$$
Both integrals are finite because the test and all its derivatives are bounded
and compactly supported. The test identity is choice-free. By
[[def-locally-integrable-function-as-a-regular-distribution]] and the signed
transpose convention in [[def-distributional-derivative]], it is equivalent
to $\partial^\alpha T_u=T_v$ as distributions. For $\alpha=0$, this identity
reduces to $T_u=T_v$, hence to $u=v$ almost everywhere by the published
embedding theorem under [[def-countable-choice]].

**Well-definedness.** Changing either representative on a null set leaves each
test integral unchanged. Weak derivatives are therefore statements about
almost-everywhere classes; existence and uniqueness of their locally
integrable value classes are audited separately.

For a distribution $u\in\mathcal D'(\Omega)$ in the convention of [[def-distribution]] and a multi-index $\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^n$, its **distributional derivative** is
$$\langle\partial^\alpha u,\varphi\rangle=(-1)^{|\alpha|}\langle u,\partial^\alpha\varphi\rangle\qquad(\varphi\in\mathcal D(\Omega)).$$
The test derivative is a continuous linear endomorphism by [[thm-test-function-operations-are-continuous]]. Its composition with $u$, multiplied by the indicated sign, is therefore a continuous complex-linear functional, so this definition produces a distribution. The pairing is bilinear, with no complex conjugation. For $\alpha=0$ the operation is the identity; for one coordinate derivative its sign is minus. Every derivative of the zero distribution is zero, including on the empty domain. No choice axiom enters this construction. Compatibility with classical derivatives requires an integration-by-parts argument where it is used; it is not part of the definition.

Assume Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$), with the exact meaning of [[def-countable-choice]]. Let $a>0$ and let $\rho\in L^1(\mathbb R^3;\mathbb R)$ vanish outside $\overline B_a(0)$. Use the complete orthonormal basis $\{Y_{lm}\}$ of real spherical harmonics on $S^2$ with unnormalised surface measure $d\sigma$ of total mass $4\pi$ and the addition theorem of [[lem-em-spherical-harmonic-basis-and-addition]], and the Legendre generating kernel and its compact remainder bound from [[lem-em-convergent-legendre-kernel]]. Write $x=rn$, $r=|x|$, $n\in S^2$. Then:

(a) **Exterior multipole expansion.** For every $x$ with $|x|>a$, $$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\frac{\rho(y)}{|x-y|}\,dy=\sum_{l=0}^\infty\sum_{m=1}^{2l+1}\frac{4\pi}{2l+1}\frac{Y_{lm}(n)}{r^{l+1}}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)\rho(y)\,dy,$$ the series converging absolutely and uniformly on $\{|x|\ge r_0\}$ for every $r_0>a$, with tail after degree $N$ bounded by $\|\rho\|_1\,a^{N+1}/(r_0^{N+2}(1-a/r_0))$; for every fixed $r>a$, the degree-$l$ term is the $L^2(S^2,d\sigma)$ angular projection of $n\mapsto F_r(n):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}|rn-y|^{-1}\rho(y)\,dy$ onto the degree-$l$ harmonics. This function is continuous and bounded by $\|\rho\|_1/(r-a)$, so it is in $L^2(S^2)$; no sphere trace or $L^2$ property of the volume density $\rho$ is asserted. The degree-zero and degree-one terms are the Coulomb and dipole terms with the explicit remainder bound of [[lem-em-coulomb-dipole-remainder]] ($Q=\int\rho$, $p=\int y\rho(y)\,dy$, $|R(x)|\le16a^2\|\rho\|_1/|x|^3$ for $|x|\ge2a$).

(b) **Termwise differentiation.** On every compact $K$ with $\inf_K|x|>a$ the series may be differentiated termwise to every order, the differentiated series converging uniformly on $K$; in particular the potential is $C^\infty$ on $\{|x|>a\}$.

(c) **Ball boundary branch.** For $f\in L^2(S^2)$ with coefficients $f_{lm}$ the series $u(rn)=\sum_{l,m}r^lf_{lm}Y_{lm}(n)$ converges in $L^2(S^2)$ as $r\uparrow1$ and, with all derivatives, uniformly on each closed ball of radius $<1$, is harmonic on the open unit ball, and is the unique harmonic function there with a finite $\sup_{r<1}\|u(r\cdot)\|_2$ and $L^2$ boundary limit $f$; for continuous $f$ it equals the Poisson integral $(1-r^2)/(4\pi|rn-n'|^3)$ of $f$ and extends continuously to the closed ball with boundary values $f$.

This is a statement about the Newtonian integral of a compactly supported $L^1$ density and about harmonic functions; no physical charge distribution or electrostatic interpretation is asserted. In every coefficient integral the factor $|y|^lY_{lm}(y/|y|)$ is defined at $y=0$ by its homogeneous polynomial extension: zero for $l\ge1$ and the constant degree-zero harmonic for $l=0$. This is a finite assignment, and changing its value at that null singleton changes no integral.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.
